preregistration.title: PRE-REGISTRATION -- verifier-scoring scope for the 2026-08-13 decoding sweep
preregistration.written_at: 2026-08-13, BEFORE any SELECTED or sel_eff number for any swept setting existed
preregistration.why: The frozen incumbent verifier must be run under HF transformers at batch 1 (vLLM drops visual.* LoRA modules), which measures ~1.5 candidates/s on a shared A100. Scoring all 42 pools was not affordable in the available GPU window, which was additionally contended by two sibling jobs. Rather than score whichever settings happened to look good, the scope is fixed in advance by a rule that does not depend on any selection outcome.

two_tiers.coverage_tier: EVERY generated setting. Needs judge labels only. Endpoints: oracle@8, distinct-candidate count, Lincoln-Petersen capture-recapture ceiling, oracle-vs-N curve, generated-token audit, per-cell oracle.
two_tiers.selection_tier: A pre-specified SUBSET. Needs the frozen verifier. Endpoints: sel_eff, SELECTED accuracy, contested-stratum and laterality-stratum SELECTED, and all paired deltas vs the matched control.

selection_tier_membership_rule: 1. T07 -- the matched control (the deployed setting, regenerated in this session). Mandatory.

2. The setting with the HIGHEST measured oracle@8 among all swept settings, ranked on judge labels alone. Rationale: SELECTED = oracle@8 x sel_eff exactly, so the setting with the largest coverage gain is the one with the best chance of converting into a SELECTED gain. If it does not convert, no smaller coverage gain can.

3. rp11 (repetition_penalty = 1.10). Rationale: a MECHANISTIC harm check fixed in advance, not an outcome-dependent pick. vLLM applies repetition_penalty to tokens in the PROMPT as well as the output (vllm/model_executor/layers/utils.py, apply_penalties -> apply_repetition_penalties(logits, prompt_mask, output_mask, ...)), and on medical VQA the correct short answer is frequently a word of the question ('left', 'right', 'upper', ...). The deployed value is 1.0, so the deployed system takes no harm; the pre-registered prediction is that raising it HURTS, concentrated in the laterality stratum.
4. If GPU time remains after those three, add settings in this fixed order: minp01, T13, T10, T03, T05, minp005, rp105, T13minp010, topk20, topk50, topp09, topp095.

prediction_registered_in_advance.temperature: oracle@8 and distinct-candidate count increase monotonically with temperature; SELECTED does NOT, because sel_eff falls with pool noise. Basis: the project's measured marginal conversion of newly-covered questions is 0.447 [0.368, 0.526], well under 1.
prediction_registered_in_advance.repetition_penalty: rp > 1.0 LOWERS SELECTED, with the damage concentrated on the laterality stratum, because vLLM penalises prompt tokens.
prediction_registered_in_advance.min_p: min_p truncates the tail, so distinct-candidate count and oracle@8 fall slightly while sel_eff rises slightly; net SELECTED approximately flat.
prediction_registered_in_advance.overall: no single-variable decoding change beats the deployed T=0.7 default on SELECTED accuracy.

decoding_sweep_currency_audit.py -- WHY does a setting win under the LLM judge and lose under
exact match?
GRADING_CURRENCY_AUDIT.judge: src/labeling/run_judge.py -- MedVLThinker-32B-RL_m23k (Qwen2.5-32B backbone: a NEUTRAL grader, not the Lingshu model under test), text-only, temperature 0, Yes/No logit comparison. The project's own judge, reused unmodified.
GRADING_CURRENCY_AUDIT.judge_system_prompt_verbatim: You are a strict medical exam grader. Given a question, a reference (gold) answer, and a model answer, decide if the model answer is CORRECT: it must match the clinical meaning of the reference. Be lenient about phrasing, synonyms, and abbreviations (e.g. 'CT' = 'computed tomography'), but mark wrong answers, missing key findings, or different conclusions as No. Respond with only 'Yes' or 'No'.
GRADING_CURRENCY_AUDIT.WHY_THE_PROMPT_MATTERS: the judge is INSTRUCTED to 'be lenient about phrasing, synonyms and abbreviations'. Judge-minus-EM disagreement is therefore by DESIGN, not a defect. The consequence for this sweep is the point: a decoding change that increases phrasing variation harvests more of that designed leniency WITHOUT the model becoming more accurate, so a judge-only gain is not evidence of better generation. That is why every headline here is reported in both currencies.

PARAPHRASE_MECHANISM_TEST.title: Does repetition_penalty win under the judge by PARAPHRASING instead of quoting?
PARAPHRASE_MECHANISM_TEST.mechanism:
vLLM applies repetition_penalty to tokens present in the PROMPT as well as the
output (vllm/model_executor/layers/utils.py: apply_penalties -> apply_repetition_penalties(logits,
prompt_mask, output_mask, ...)). The prompt contains the question. In these three open VQA sets the gold
answer very often REUSES a word of the question ('Which lung is affected?' -> 'right lung'). So
repetition_penalty > 1 should push the model away from quoting the question and toward SYNONYMS.

That predicts exactly the observed sign flip:
  * normalised exact match is LEXICAL -- a synonym scores 0                      -> EM falls
  * the 32B judge is SEMANTIC -- a synonym scores 1                             -> judge holds/rises
so the setting looks like a coverage WIN under the judge and a LOSS under EM without the model having
become any better at the task.
PARAPHRASE_MECHANISM_TEST.stratifier: GOLD shares >=1 content word with the QUESTION (stopword-filtered, computed once on the control pool T07_s0 so it is identical across settings)
PARAPHRASE_MECHANISM_TEST.POWER_WARNING_P3: the gold-shares-a-question-word stratum holds only 92 of 2345 items, so each item moves the EM-oracle by 1/92 = 0.0109 and the P3 contrast is UNDERPOWERED. P3 is reported but is NOT evidence either way.

COVERAGE_CEILING_PER_SETTING.title: Capture-recapture coverage ceiling PER DECODING SETTING
COVERAGE_CEILING_PER_SETTING.question: the +0.0091 macro free bound was measured on the deployed distribution; does it move when the decoding distribution moves?
COVERAGE_CEILING_PER_SETTING.estimator: Lincoln-Petersen over two independent generation seeds of the SAME setting (8 samples each), judge-labelled. LOWER BOUND: per-item heterogeneity biases LP down.
COVERAGE_CEILING_PER_SETTING.currency_caveat: computed in the JUDGE currency. _decoding_sweep_currency_audit.json shows the judge credits verbose answers that exact match rejects, so ceilings for verbose settings (rp11, T13) are upper-leaning.

VALIDATION_against_published_bound.note: same arithmetic, the project's own constants. At TWO seeds (one Lincoln-Petersen pair) this reproduced the published +0.0091 to 4 dp (0.009058). At THREE seeds (three LP pairs, lower variance) the control gives +0.0087. The difference is LP seed-pair spread, not a disagreement: both round to +0.009. The 3-seed value is the better estimate and is what the per_setting rows use. This reproduces the published VALUE; it is not a claim to have re-run the original derivation path.

FINDING.reading: the iid-resampling ceiling MOVES with the decoding distribution: hotter sampling raises it, colder sampling lowers it. But a higher ceiling was NOT harvestable -- the setting with the highest ceiling (T13) has the WORST measured SELECTED accuracy, because per-slot accuracy and sel_eff both fall faster than coverage rises. This is the project's recurring luck-floor shape: more reachable, not more reached.

temperature.registered: oracle@8 and distinct-candidate count increase monotonically with temperature; SELECTED does NOT, because sel_eff falls with pool noise. Basis: the project's measured marginal conversion of newly-covered questions is 0.447 [0.368, 0.526], well under 1.
temperature.VERDICT: PARTLY REFUTED: distinct-candidate count does rise monotonically with temperature, but oracle@8 does NOT -- it PEAKS at the deployed T=0.7 and falls on both sides. More diversity stops buying coverage past 0.7 because per-sample accuracy falls faster than diversity helps. The SELECTED half of the prediction (that it does not rise WITH temperature) held -- but the fuller ladder shows SELECTED peaks at T05, i.e. BELOW the deployed 0.7, so 'no temperature change helps' would be the wrong lesson.

repetition_penalty.registered: rp > 1.0 LOWERS SELECTED, with the damage concentrated on the laterality stratum, because vLLM penalises prompt tokens.
repetition_penalty.why_not: run_openvqa.py never sets repetition_penalty, so vLLM's default 1.0 applies and NO penalty is computed. Verified by resolving SamplingParams(temperature=0.7, max_tokens=64, n=8, logprobs=5) -> repetition_penalty=1.0.
repetition_penalty.VERDICT: REFUTED IN THE REGISTERED DIRECTION, AND NOT A WIN EITHER. rp=1.10 did not lower SELECTED and did not damage the laterality stratum (TIE). It RAISED judge-currency SELECTED by +0.00483 (WIN) while LOWERING exact-match SELECTED by -0.00768 (LOSS). The registered harm mechanism (vLLM penalising prompt tokens) is real -- rp11 measurably quotes the question less -- but it did not produce the registered harm.

min_p.registered: min_p truncates the tail, so distinct-candidate count and oracle@8 fall slightly while sel_eff rises slightly; net SELECTED approximately flat.
min_p.VERDICT: CONFIRMED. min_p=0.10 cut oracle@8 (0.6060 vs 0.6286) and distinct candidates (2.98 vs 3.67) while RAISING sel_eff (0.8002 vs 0.7652), leaving SELECTED at +0.00398 (TIE) in the judge currency. Exactly the registered trade.

overall.registered: no single-variable decoding change beats the deployed T=0.7 default on SELECTED accuracy.
overall.VERDICT: REFUTED. T05 beat(s) the deployed T=0.7 default on SELECTED accuracy CI-cleanly in BOTH grading currencies. The registered prediction was right about the MECHANISM it had in mind (extra diversity does not pay) but wrong about the conclusion, because it only considered making the pool RICHER. Moving the other way -- a COLDER, less diverse pool -- raises sel_eff more than it costs coverage, and that is where the win is. Magnitude is modest and its 8-cell macro share leans on vqa_rad_open (n=200): see HEADLINE_2026_08_14..HOW_BIG_IS_THE_WIN in the primary artifact.

HEADLINE_2026_08_14.endpoint: SELECTED accuracy on the frozen 2,345-item open pool, frozen incumbent verifier
HEADLINE_2026_08_14.control: T07 = the deployed setting (temperature 0.7, every other sampling field at the vLLM default), REGENERATED in-session; all deltas are against it, never against a stored number.

per_setting_dual_currency.classification: WEAKLY POSITIVE (CI-clean in one currency, TIE in the other; never negative)
CURRENCY CONFLICT (CI-clean opposite signs -- a grading effect, not a generation one)
WEAKLY POSITIVE (CI-clean in one currency, TIE in the other; never negative)
WEAKLY NEGATIVE (CI-clean loss in one currency, TIE in the other)

HEADLINE_2026_08_14.verdict: ROBUST WIN FOUND: ['T05'] beat(s) the deployed control on SELECTED accuracy CI-cleanly in BOTH grading currencies. The rest of the grid splits into CURRENCY CONFLICT ['rp11'] (CI-clean WIN under the LLM judge, CI-clean LOSS under exact match -- a grading effect, not a generation one), WEAKLY POSITIVE ['T03', 'minp01'], and CLEAR LOSS ['T10', 'T13'].

HOW_BIG_IS_THE_WIN.caveat: the pooled open-pool endpoint and the project's 8-cell MACRO answer different questions, and they disagree in magnitude here. Both are reported; neither is suppressed.
HOW_BIG_IS_THE_WIN.pooled_open_pool_n2345: the headline endpoint of this sweep -- CI-clean in both currencies.
HOW_BIG_IS_THE_WIN.macro_8cell: T=0.5 contributes +0.00415 to the 8-cell macro, but 75% of that comes from vqa_rad_open (n=200), the smallest and noisiest cell, which macro weighting promotes to 1/8. EXCLUDING that cell the macro contribution is +0.00103 -- BELOW the project's own +0.0029 significance threshold. So this is a real, reproducible, zero-cost gain on the open arm, NOT a macro-headline result.
HOW_BIG_IS_THE_WIN.seed_stability: per-seed matched SELECTED deltas for T=0.5 are [-0.00085, +0.00896, +0.00896]: two of three seeds clearly positive, one essentially zero. Seed sd of SELECTED is 0.0021, the tightest in the grid.
HOW_BIG_IS_THE_WIN.guardrail: guardrail-CLEAN: no cell is negative (slake +0.00465 TIE, vqa_rad +0.02500 WIN, pathvqa +0.00356 TIE).
HOW_BIG_IS_THE_WIN.contested_stratum: +0.01736 [+0.00592, +0.02959] WIN -- CI-clean on the sensitive secondary endpoint (n=845).

THE_MECHANISM_THAT_MATTERS.finding: the settings that help do so by RAISING sel_eff while LOWERING coverage -- the opposite of the coverage hypothesis this sweep was launched to test.
THE_MECHANISM_THAT_MATTERS.evidence: T=0.3 has the LOWEST oracle@8 of any setting measured (0.5588 vs the control's 0.6286, a CI-clean coverage LOSS) and yet the HIGHEST SELECTED accuracy, because sel_eff rises from 0.7652 to 0.8704 (+0.105). SELECTED = oracle@8 x sel_eff exactly, so a -11.1% relative coverage change against a +13.7% relative sel_eff change nets positive.
THE_MECHANISM_THAT_MATTERS.why_it_makes_sense: the project's own measured marginal conversion of NEWLY-COVERED questions is 0.447 [0.368, 0.526] -- coverage gains convert at well under 1 -- whereas a proportional sel_eff gain converts at exactly 1 by the identity. Making the candidate pool EASIER TO SELECT FROM is therefore worth more per unit than making it richer.
THE_MECHANISM_THAT_MATTERS.consequence_for_the_coverage_attack: changing the candidate distribution IS a real lever, but it paid off in the selection term, not the coverage term. More diversity (T=1.3: distinct 5.48 vs 3.67) bought neither: it lost coverage AND sel_eff.
